dedupe_keys.name: building topology ontology bot w3c linked building data community group

description: The Building Topology Ontology (BOT) is a minimal OWL DL ontology for the core topological concepts of a building, prepared by the W3C Linked Building Data Community Group as a public draft following W3C conventions, so that sensors, products and devices can be described in the context of the building they sit in and buildings can be linked into smart city data. It defines zones (Site, Building, Storey and Space), building Elements and Interfaces, with object properties such as hasBuilding, hasStorey, hasSpace, containsElement, adjacentElement, adjacentZone, intersectsZone, hasSubElement, interfaceOf and has3DModel, and a datatype property for simple 3D models; the namespace is https://w3id.org/bot#. The ontology file gives version 0.3.2, issued June 2018 and modified July 2020. Coverage: any building, not tied to a place. Access: free specification and Turtle file. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution. Caveats: deliberately minimal, so domain detail comes from aligned ontologies such as Brick or RealEstateCore; it remains a community group draft, not a W3C standard. Simulation uses: a shared spatial backbone linking BIM, sensor and simulation data in building digital twins. Related records: Brick, RealEstateCore and the Azure DTDL version of RealEstateCore.
